key_takeaways: Write the consistency specification for the chosen N, W and R; components alone do not define a guarantee.
Version every write and reconcile by version with read repair, never by wall-clock time.
A rejoining node recovers from its co-owners before it serves reads.

exercise.title: Deliver the model, traces and specification
exercise.instructions: Complete the model with versioned writes, quorum reads with read repair, recovery on rejoin and a stable ring; write three executable failure traces (owner leaves mid-write, stale rejoin, partition across owners) that assert or document the guarantee; and write SPEC.md with N, W, R, the guarantees provided and not provided, the reconciliation rule and the recovery protocol.
exercise.deliverable: src/model.mjs, three passing or documented failure traces, and SPEC.md.
hints: Recovery is: ask co-owners, keep the highest version per key, replay your own log for keys they lack.
Read repair writes the winning version back to stale replicas after a read.
State in SPEC.md what happens when two writers produce the same version number.

questions.prompt: With N = 3, W = 2 and R = 2, why does a read after a completed write return the new value even if one owner is down?
choices: Because all three replicas always agree
Because W + R > N guarantees the read overlaps a replica that acknowledged the write
Because the down node is skipped
questions.correct_answer: Because W + R > N guarantees the read overlaps a replica that acknowledged the write
questions.explanation: Quorum overlap is the mechanism; the read picks the highest version among its replies.

questions.prompt: Two replicas hold different versions of a key after a partition. Which reconciliation rule does the lab require?
choices: The higher version wins, then read repair updates the stale replica
The replica with more keys wins
questions.correct_answer: The higher version wins, then read repair updates the stale replica
questions.explanation: Versions, not clocks, order writes; read repair converges replicas.

questions.prompt: What must a rejoining node do before serving reads?
choices: Recover the newest versions from its co-owners and replay its own log
questions.correct_answer: Recover the newest versions from its co-owners and replay its own log
questions.explanation: Serving before recovery returns stale data with a valid-looking version.

questions.prompt: The team sets W = 1 and R = 1 for latency and writes 'consistent' in the spec. Explain what the spec should say instead.
questions.correct_answer: With W + R not exceeding N, a read may hit a replica that never saw the write, so the store offers no read-your-writes or monotonic-reads guarantee for that configuration; it is eventually consistent per key with convergence through read repair and anti-entropy. The spec must name those session guarantees as not provided and describe how clients handle stale reads, or raise W and R until quorums overlap.
questions.explanation: Guarantees follow from N, W and R, not from the word consistent.

questions.prompt: Why does the model refuse to provide linearizability across concurrent writers without a coordinator, and what would add it?
questions.correct_answer: Two writers can assign versions independently and reach different replicas first, so there is no single real-time order that all reads observe; the quorum only guarantees overlap, not a total order. Linearizability needs a serialization point: a per-key leader or a consensus protocol that orders writes before they are applied, at the cost of availability under partition.
questions.learning_objective: Explain the limit of quorum-based stores
